source.name: The ABCs of City Planning (NYC Department of City Planning, 2026)

terms.def: When the cost of living meets people's needs, so residents can stay in the city and succeed.
Places of business that provide jobs, food and shopping.
How many people live together in a place. As cities grow denser, more people come together in the same area.
A measure that tells you how big a building is allowed to be.
Places where things are made, from factories to workshops, where ideas take physical shape.
Small vehicles such as scooters and bikes that people use for quick trips.
A plan for a neighborhood's future that the community develops together.
Land where no buildings stand, on grass, pavement or sand, used for growing things, play and relaxation.
The places where people live, from row houses to high rises, built of brick, concrete and stone.
Reducing pollution and waste to make the city a green, healthy place.
The ways people get around the city, including subways, buses and bikes.
The design of the city that shapes public space, so people feel at home wherever they go.
Where the city meets the water. New York City has 520 miles of waterfront.
Combining shops, homes and offices in the same building.
The rules for how land is used, so the city grows in a well-planned way.
